title: useRef Hook

theory.english: useRef returns a mutable ref object whose .current property is initialized to the passed argument. Unlike state, mutating a ref does not trigger a re-render. Refs have two main uses: 1) Accessing DOM elements directly (like focusing an input, playing a video), and 2) Storing any mutable value that you want to persist across renders without triggering re-renders (like a timer ID, previous value, or render count).
theory.hindi: useRef ek mutable ref object return karta hai jiska .current property passed argument se initialize hoti hai. State ke unlike, ref mutate karne se re-render trigger nahi hota. Refs ke do main uses hain: 1) DOM elements ko directly access karna (jaise input focus karna, video play karna), aur 2) Koi bhi mutable value store karna jo renders ke beech persist kare bina re-render trigger kiye.
theory.hinglish: useRef se DOM elements ko directly access karo ya values store karo jo re-render trigger nahi karte. ref.current se value read/write karo. Input focus karna, timer ID store karna, previous value track karna — sab ke liye useRef use karo.

examples.title: DOM Access and Value Persistence
examples.explanation: inputRef.current gives direct access to the DOM input element. renderCount.current tracks renders without itself causing a re-render.

exercises.prompt: Create a component with a video element. Add Play and Pause buttons that control the video using useRef.
exercises.expectedOutcome: useRef pointing to the video element, buttons calling ref.current.play() and ref.current.pause().

quiz.question: What happens when you change a ref's .current value?
quiz.explanation: Mutating ref.current does not cause a re-render. This is the key difference between refs and state.

quiz.question: How do you attach a ref to a DOM element?
quiz.explanation: Pass the ref object using the ref prop on any JSX element to attach it to the underlying DOM node.

quiz.question: What is a good use case for useRef (NOT for DOM access)?
options: Storing a setInterval ID to clear it later
quiz.explanation: Storing a timer ID in a ref lets you clear it later without causing re-renders when the ID is stored.

summary: useRef chapter complete! Aapne seekha DOM elements access karna, render-safe mutable values store karna, aur ref vs state ka difference.
